patterns.platform: Elementor Form widget / Divi Contact Form / WPForms — submission feedback
patterns.name: Success/error toast not in a live region; errors flagged by color only
patterns.description: After AJAX form submit, the success or error message is injected into a <div> that is not a live region and not focused, so screen readers never announce it. Inline validation marks invalid fields with a red border/red text only, with no programmatic error association and no text describing what's wrong or how to fix it.
patterns.typicalMarkup: Your message was sent!
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: The success div is valid HTML; nothing in the static DOM signals it should announce on change. Detecting that a dynamically-inserted status isn't announced requires triggering the submit and observing AT silence. Color-only error indication also needs visual judgment that no text/icon backs the red.
patterns.realWorldNote: ARIA live-region guidance: 'create an empty element and then update its content' — builder messages don't. https://a11y-blog.dev/en/articles/aria-live-regions/ ; matches harness 4.1.3 / 3.3.x shadow lanes.

patterns.platform: React conditionally-rendered form error summary / aria-live status
patterns.name: Submit-time errors rendered but not announced; focus not moved
patterns.description: On form submit, a React app conditionally renders an error summary or per-field messages into the DOM, but the container is not a live region and focus is not moved to it. Sighted users see red errors; screen-reader users get no announcement and remain focused on the submit button, unaware the submission failed.
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: The error text is present in the post-submit DOM, so a snapshot scan sees content, not a failure. Whether it was ANNOUNCED (live region) or focus was moved to it is a dynamic, interaction-and-timing property invisible to static/single-snapshot tools.
patterns.realWorldNote: TetraLogical and Up Your A11y describe accessible error-summary patterns requiring focus management or a live region; conditionally-rendered React errors routinely omit both. https://tetralogical.com/blog/2024/10/21/foundations-form-validation-and-error-messages/

patterns.platform: Contact/checkout forms in Gravity Forms, Wix Forms, Shopify checkout, HubSpot forms
patterns.name: Required state and errors conveyed by color/asterisk only, not programmatically
patterns.description: Required fields are marked with a red asterisk or red border (color/symbol only) with no required/aria-required and no legend explaining the asterisk. On submit, errors are shown as red text near fields but not associated via aria-describedby and the field gets no aria-invalid, so screen readers never learn the field is required, that it errored, or what the message says.
patterns.typicalMarkup: Invalid email
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: A bare visible label may satisfy the form-label check, but tools cannot tell that requiredness/error is conveyed by COLOR alone (1.4.1), cannot verify an error message is the CORRECT suggestion (3.3.3), and cannot confirm the on-submit error text is programmatically tied to the field — these need a human to submit the form and inspect the associations and meaning.
patterns.realWorldNote: WebAIM Million 2026: missing form labels on 51% of pages (top error): https://webaim.org/projects/million/ ; required-field color-only guidance: https://www.deque.com/blog/aria-requiredtrue-wcag-2-compliance-practice/

patterns.platform: Required fields and inline validation in form builders / SPA forms where required and error state are visual-only (red border, red asterisk) without aria-required / aria-invalid / aria-describedby
patterns.name: form error and required state not programmatically associated
patterns.description: A field is marked required with a red asterisk and, on submit, an error appears as red text below it — but the input has no aria-required, no aria-invalid="true", and the error message is not tied via aria-describedby. Screen-reader users do not learn the field is required, that it errored, or what the suggested fix is.
patterns.typicalMarkup: Enter a valid email
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: The error markup is valid HTML and the field has a label, so structural scans pass. The failure is the missing programmatic ASSOCIATION between input, its required/invalid state, and the message text — which only surfaces by submitting the form (a dynamic step) and judging whether the announced output conveys the error and a suggestion; scanners do not trigger validation or evaluate message quality.
patterns.realWorldNote: WCAG 3.3.1/3.3.3 and reform.app 'Common ARIA Mistakes in Forms'; red-asterisk-only required and unassociated inline errors are among the most common audited form failures. https://www.reform.app/blog/common-aria-mistakes-in-forms-and-fixes
